title: Trailing comma is the line-continuation character, including inside argument lists
purpose: Prevent silent blank-concatenation of the next line's token onto the current one, which produces a value that is subtly wrong rather than a syntax error.
trigger: A line ends with a bare trailing comma. In ooRexx a trailing comma at the end of ANY line continues that logical line onto the next -- this applies inside a multi-line method-call argument list exactly as it does anywhere else, which is easy to miss coming from languages where a trailing comma in an argument list is either meaningless or an explicit multi-element separator convention.
correct: Either keep every argument of one call on a single line, or build intermediate variables and pass them, rather than relying on a trailing comma to continue an argument list across lines.
compiler_relationship: This is standard ooRexx line-continuation syntax working exactly as specified; the rule exists because the specific consequence inside an argument list is non-obvious, not because the language is misbehaving.
return_semantics: A LanguageRulePage may be opened and then return to the originating cycle selector.
